drhp.business: Deep Industries Limited supplies equipment and services to oil and gas field operations on rental, charter-hire and dry-lease terms rather than selling assets outright. It began with natural gas compression in the 1990s and has added gas dehydration, drilling and workover rigs, integrated project management, charter hire of entire gas processing facilities, offshore support services and, most recently, production enhancement of mature fields. risks.note: Named by the Company in both the MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' paragraph and the BRSR material-issues table: being in a niche services segment related to the oil and gas industry, where only a few companies are present in the country, the Company sees a risk of dependency on few clients. Stated mitigation is expanding the customer base outside the country. Financial implication flagged as negative.
risks.risk: Customer concentration - dependency on a few clients

risks.note: Flagged in the MD&A and repeated as a BRSR material issue with negative financial implications. The business model is asset-led charter hire, so failure to source correctly specified rigs, compressors and dehydration packages on time directly constrains contract execution. Stated mitigation is continuous training programmes and staying updated on the latest equipment availability.
risks.risk: Procurement risk - inability to procure rightly configured equipment in a timely manner

risks.note: Listed first among the Company's concerns in the MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' paragraph. The services are manpower-intensive and technical; the Company responds by appointing experienced professionals in technical and commercial departments and, as a stated strategic policy, hiring a new pool of talent every year from reputed technical/petroleum institutes through campus selection.
risks.risk: Scarcity of skilled personnel in the market

risks.note: The MD&A states that, being a service provider to a high risk industry, safety of employees is the utmost priority and that the Company ensures compliance with all rules and regulations while providing services. Worker training in the year covered fire safety, mines vocational training and first-aid. The Health, Safety & Environment paragraph is cut off mid-word in this bundle, so the full disclosure could not be read.
risks.risk: Safety exposure as a service provider to a high-risk industry

risks.note: The whole growth narrative rests on Indian upstream activity, PSU outsourcing and government policy support, with no offsetting business line disclosed. The MD&A's own discussion of financial performance reports revenue under a single nature-of-services description, and management describes the segment as one in which only a few companies operate in the country - so both demand and competition are concentrated.
risks.risk: Single-industry exposure to Indian oil & gas capex and policy

risks.note: BRSR Section B item 9 states the Company does not currently have dedicated Board-level leadership for sustainability related issues; the CSR, Risk Management and Stakeholder Relationship Committees look at broader ESG aspects under Board guidance. Item 11 states no independent assessment or evaluation of the working of its policies has been carried out by an external agency for any of the nine principles.
risks.risk: No dedicated Board-level ownership of sustainability, and no independent assessment of policies

risks.note: BRSR Section B item 3 answers 'No' for all nine NGRBC principles on whether the enlisted policies extend to value chain partners. For a contractor deploying equipment and manpower at client wellsites, conduct and HSE exposure in the supply chain is left outside the policy perimeter.
risks.risk: ESG policies do not extend to value-chain partners

risks.note: An Independent Director, Mr. Ashok Ratilal Patel, ceased to be a director on his demise on 13th December 2025 and was replaced by Mr. Shalin Harshadbhai Patel with effect from 12th March 2026, whose regularisation was passed by members only on 27th April 2026. The Board's Report also records the Company Secretary, Mrs. Shilpa Sharma, as holding office upto 31st July 2026, i.e. a KMP departure after the balance-sheet date.
